title: The Best Time To Send A Cold Email
author: Tom
excerpt: Tuesday through Thursday, mid morning, recipient's time zone. That part is the easy answer. The part that actually decides whether the email gets read is not about timing at all.

title: What To Put In A Follow-Up Email After A Sales Call
author: Tom
excerpt: Most follow-up emails get ignored because they skip one of three things, a recap, a dated next step, and a reason to reply beyond checking in. Here is what to put in instead.

title: AI Didn't Replace The Thinking This Week. It Replaced The Typing.
author: Tom
excerpt: People assume AI tools mean cutting corners. Here is what a week of building with them actually looked like, and what still has to come from a person.

title: Why Reply Rate Is the Wrong Number to Judge Cold Email On
author: Tom
excerpt: Published benchmarks range from 0.45% to 5%, depending entirely on who is counting and what they count. Here is what the number hides, and the four you should steer by instead.

title: How Long Does Cold Email Warm-Up Actually Take?
author: Tom
excerpt: The ramp takes three to four weeks. The runway from registering a domain to sending anything that matters is closer to eight. Those are two different questions, and the tools answer the first one when you asked the second.

title: The Five Layers of a B2B Outbound System, and Where They Break
author: Tom
excerpt: Domains, warm-up, lead data, sequencing, reply handling. Four right and one wrong and the whole thing underperforms, and you will not know which layer did it. Here is the failure mode for each.

title: Why most outbound fails before the first email sends
author: Tom
excerpt: The part everyone skips is the part that decides whether anything gets read. A short note on deliverability, warm-up, and the eight weeks nobody wants to hear about.
